pointers.sentence: The docstring of `parse_html` gives the aim, a structure "that can be easily compared against other HTML on semantic equivalence" (`django/test/html.py:parse_html`).
`parse_html` feeds the string to a `Parser`, a subclass of `html.parser.HTMLParser` that keeps a root and a stack of the elements still open (`django/test/html.py:Parser`).

A start tag makes an `Element`, appends it to the innermost open element, or the root, and pushes it on the stack unless its name is in `VOID_ELEMENTS`, the elements without content (`django/utils/html.py:VOID_ELEMENTS`).
An end tag pops the stack until it has popped an element of its own name, closing whatever it passes (`django/test/html.py:Parser.handle_endtag`).

`parse_html` then finalises the tree and returns the root's only child where the root holds one element and no text; otherwise the `RootElement`, a nameless element that prints as its children (`django/test/html.py:RootElement`).

An `Element` is a name, a sorted list of attributes, and a list of children, each an element or a string; two are equal when their names, attributes and children, in order, are (`django/test/html.py:Element.__eq__`).
**Attributes** pass through `normalize_attributes` and are sorted, so their order does not count (`django/test/html.py:Element.__init__`, `django/test/html.py:normalize_attributes`).
**Attributes** pass through `normalize_attributes` and are sorted, so their order does not count (`django/test/html.py:Element.__init__`, `django/test/html.py:normalize_attributes`).
**Text** is normalised as it is appended (`django/test/html.py:Element.append`): each run of ASCII white space becomes one space, and neighbouring text is joined.

`assertHTMLEqual` parses each side through `assert_and_parse_html`, which turns a parse error into a failure naming the argument, and fails when the trees differ, showing both, each cut past 80 characters, and a `difflib.ndiff` of their lines unless it is longer than `unittest.TestCase.maxDiff` (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertHTMLEqual`).
`assertInHTML` parses both and counts the needle in the haystack with `Element.count` (`django/test/html.py:Element._count`).
With `count=None` one match is enough, and otherwise the number must be exact; `SimpleTestCase.assertNotInHTML` (5.1) asks for none (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertInHTML`).

`assertJSONEqual` parses its first argument with `json.loads`, which takes bytes as well as a string, and its second only if it is a string, so the example can pass a dictionary (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.assertJSONEqual`).
